audit.whatIsWrong: The page's entire focus is an ability that does not exist: "Subject: Fear (CC Paints)" appears in focus.text, winCon, enemyWin, loading (twice), breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.feeding, dosFull[0].d, dosFull[2].d, report[1].t, report[3].t, report[5].t and report[9].t. Separately, the content layer names sub-spells that are also wrong — "QW pool", "QQ meteor", "EW disintegrate", "EE root", "Q1 fireball".
audit.why: Hwei's crowd-control palette is Subject: Torment (E), 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, which replaces his abilities with Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss and Crushing Maw. There is no ability called Subject: Fear. The pool the content layer puts on the Q palette is Pool of Reflection and it belongs to Subject: Serenity (W); the damage paints belong to Subject: Disaster (Q). The packet flagged this matchup as never naming any of Hwei's abilities correctly, and it is the single worst defect on the page — the reader is told to track a cooldown that has no name in the game.
audit.corrected: Every instance replaced with Subject: Torment, Subject: Disaster, Subject: Serenity or Spiraling Despair as appropriate, with the real per-rank cooldowns attached.

audit.whatIsWrong: Signature of the Visionary is never mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: Hwei primes a champion he damages, and a second damaging spell completes the signature, which then detonates under them after a short delay. That is the whole trading rule of this lane for an immobile mage: the first paint is survivable, the second is the one that kills. It is more decisive than anything the page currently tells the reader to track.
audit.corrected: Written into enemyWin and breakdown.feeding as "do not take the second spell".

audit.whatIsWrong: Two chart rows disagreed between layers: content win[0] = Orianna against phases[0].side = Skill, and content win[3] = Hwei against phases[3].side = Skill. The packet levelChart agrees with content on both.
audit.why: Level 1 is Orianna's: a Disaster paint costs him 80 mana and needs two casts to resolve, against an 815-range Command: Attack and a stacking passive. Levels 4-5 are his: all three palettes are live, Subject: Torment is on 12s, and his poke out-ranges her setups while she has no dash to leave with.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side = Orianna at 6/10, phases[3].side = Hwei at 6/10 with phases[3].why rewritten to describe his palettes taking over rather than Orianna's Dissonance controlling the ground.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.spikes named no Hwei spike and carried an unsourced magnitude ("Luden's makes Q-W a third of a health bar").
audit.why: His spikes are Subject: Torment falling from 12s to 10s, Subject: Disaster from 10s to 6s, and Spiraling Despair arriving at level 6 with 1300 range on 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: Spike line rebuilt on the palette cooldowns and the 1300-range ultimate.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit, and the packet counts one sequencing cue on the whole matchup.
audit.why: Subject: Disaster 10/9/8/7/6 at 80-120 mana, Subject: Serenity 18/17.5/17/16.5/16 at 90-110 mana, Subject: Torment 12/11.5/11/10.5/10 at 50-70 mana, Spiraling Despair 120/100/80. His mana costs are the real early brake and nothing on the page said so.
audit.corrected: Real numbers written into breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, report[9].t, ahead, breakdown.early and the do's.

notes: This page tracked an ability that does not exist. "Subject: Fear (CC Paints)" was the matchup's focus and appeared in thirteen fields including focus.text, loading, breakdown.cooldowns and four report entries. Hwei's crowd-control palette is Subject: Torment (E, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10, replacing his abilities with Grim Visage, Gaze of the Abyss and Crushing Maw). All thirteen replaced. The content layer's sub-spell shorthand was also wrong in the other direction — it put the pool on the Q palette ("QW pool") when Pool of Reflection belongs to Subject: Serenity, and invented "disintegrate" and "meteor" for the Disaster paints. I deliberately did NOT substitute individual sub-spell names for the shorthand: hwei.json lists the three names per palette but not which input produces which, and guessing the mapping would trade one fabricated name for another. Everything is written at palette level, which is verifiable from the file. Added Signature of the Visionary, which appeared nowhere: two damaging paints on the same champion complete it and it detonates underneath them — for an immobile Orianna that is the actual trading rule of the lane, more decisive than any single cooldown. QUESTION WORTH DECIDING (did not block the audit): focus.text is 30 characters and not on the enum-exempt list, so it is length-banded like prose; I fit the replacement to exactly 30 characters ("Hwei's Subject: Torment paints") to get the fix through. If focus.text is meant to be enum-like, exempting it would let it read simply "Hwei Subject: Torment".
